items.author: bob
items.quote: Every test in `test_netcdf_reader.py` then runs against the mock, so none of them exercises the real decoding path (scale factors, `_FillValue` masking, CF time units).
items.principle: Tests must not replace a missing library with a mock that removes the real code path they claim to test.
items.rationale: The tests pass in CI only because nothing real is read.

items.author: alice
items.quote: installing system packages in CI slows every job and the reader logic is covered by the mock
items.principle: Mocking an unavailable system library is acceptable to keep CI jobs fast.
items.rationale: installing system packages in CI slows every job

items.author: bob
items.quote: if a test needs a system library that isn't there, put the library in CI. Mocking the import away just means the test checks the mock.
items.principle: When a test needs a missing system library, install it in CI rather than mocking the import.
items.rationale: The mock returns whatever we tell it to.

items.author: bob
items.quote: As a general rule, file-handling functions should take `pathlib.Path` and let callers convert at the edge
items.principle: File-handling functions take pathlib.Path, with callers converting at the edge.
items.rationale: it avoids the `str | Path` ambiguity and makes the type contract explicit.

items.author: bob
items.quote: The tests only read the first 10 records. A smaller fixture keeps the repository light and the test fast.
items.principle: Test data fixtures hold only the records the tests read.
items.rationale: A smaller fixture keeps the repository light and the test fast.

items.author: alice
items.quote: files under tests/data are small on purpose. Trim to the records the test reads; never regenerate them from a full day of output.
items.principle: Agents keep files under tests/data trimmed to the records a test reads and never regenerate them from full output.

items.author: dave
items.quote: `ds_var` -> `variable`, it's not a dataset.
items.principle: Rename ds_var to variable.
items.rationale: it's not a dataset.

items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.quote: Consider raising a descriptive error instead.
items.principle: A failed file open raises a descriptive error rather than returning None from a broad except.
items.rationale: Callers do not check for `None`, which may cause an `AttributeError` later.

items.author: dave
items.quote: let the open fail and the traceback name the file. Swallowing it is exactly the silent fallback we said we don't do.
items.principle: Do not wrap a file open in a broad except; let the failure propagate and name the file.
items.rationale: Swallowing it is exactly the silent fallback we said we don't do.

items.author: erin
items.quote: Can you add a test for a file with no `time` variable?
items.principle: Add a test for a file with no time variable.
items.rationale: I think this line raises IndexError instead of the ValueError the docstring promises.

items.author: erin
items.quote: don't assume one fill value for the whole file. Temperature uses -9999.0 but the count fields use -1, and the reader has to take `_FillValue` per variable.
items.principle: Fill values differ per variable; readers take _FillValue per variable, never one for the file.
items.rationale: Temperature uses -9999.0 but the count fields use -1

items.author: carol
items.quote: Suggested change: use `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` and format with `isoformat()`.
items.principle: Product timestamps are timezone-aware UTC, never naive.
items.rationale: The resulting string has no offset, so a consumer cannot tell whether it is UTC or local time.

items.author: erin
items.quote: Every timestamp we write is UTC and ends in `Z`, e.g. `2026-10-03T00:00:00Z`.
items.principle: Every written timestamp is UTC with a trailing Z, not +00:00.
items.rationale: Downstream parsers split on that.

items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.quote: Consider using `None` and creating the list inside the function.
items.principle: Do not use mutable default arguments; default to None and create the object inside.
items.rationale: Mutations inside `summarize` persist across calls.

items.author: carol
items.quote: Ruff has B006 for exactly this; let's enable it in pyproject and stop reviewing for it by hand.
items.principle: Enable ruff B006 so mutable defaults are caught by the linter, not by review.
items.rationale: we shouldn't need a person or a bot to spot this.

items.author: carol
items.quote: It explains a past alternative rather than the loop below it.
items.principle: A code comment describes the code below it, not alternatives that were dropped.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Comments should say what the code below them does. What we tried and dropped belongs in the commit message, not the source.
items.principle: Comments say what the code below them does; history of dropped approaches goes in the commit message.

items.author: erin
items.quote: Typo in the test name: `test_empy_day_row`.
items.principle: Fix the typo in test_empy_day_row.

items.author: carol
items.quote: Can `n_samples` be `int32` here? The product table says int32 for that column.
items.principle: Make n_samples int32 as the product table specifies.
items.rationale: The product table says int32 for that column.

items.author: dave
items.quote: a daily product never drops a day. A day with no samples still gets its row, filled, with `n_samples` = 0.
items.principle: A daily product has a row for every day; a day with no samples is filled with n_samples = 0.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Consider accepting both spellings for a release and emitting a `DeprecationWarning` for the old one.
items.principle: Renamed configuration keys keep the old spelling working for a release with a deprecation warning.
items.rationale: Renaming `outputDir` to `output_dir` will break any existing configuration file.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Agents: don't build compatibility layers for users we don't have — a rename before the first release is just a rename.
items.principle: Agents do not add compatibility layers for a library with no users yet.
items.rationale: nobody runs this library yet.

items.author: dave
items.quote: A complete changelog helps reviewers track every change.
items.principle: The changelog lists every change, internal refactors and test helpers included.
items.rationale: A complete changelog helps reviewers track every change.

items.author: dave
items.quote: The changelog is for people who use the package. Internal refactors and test helpers don't go in it; the rename does, because their config files change.
items.principle: The changelog lists only changes a package user would notice, not internal refactors or test helpers.
items.rationale: the rename does, because their config files change.

items.author: alice
items.quote: `docs/config.md` line 14 and the example on line 31 still use the old key.
items.principle: Update docs/config.md to the new key name.

items.author: bob
items.quote: Reminder to the coding agents in here: keep the diff to what the ticket asks. A rename PR is not the place to reflow docstrings.
items.principle: Agents keep a diff to what the ticket asks, with no unrelated reformatting.

items.author: erin
items.quote: Can you add a test that an unknown key raises?
items.principle: Add a test that an unknown config key raises.
items.rationale: Right now only the happy path is covered.

items.author: erin
items.quote: `cfg_d` -> `settings`?
items.principle: Rename cfg_d to settings.

items.author: carol
items.quote: rename `tmp2` to `station_tmp`, it's the only one left.
items.principle: Rename tmp2 to station_tmp.

items.author: erin
items.quote: we decided on the call that config keys are snake_case everywhere, including the YAML files users write.
items.principle: Configuration keys are snake_case everywhere, including user YAML files.

items.author: erin
items.quote: If the rounding change is correct, the expected values should be derived again by hand; if the old values were right, the code is wrong.
items.principle: Changed expected test values must be derived independently, not copied from the new output.

items.author: dave
items.quote: the new values come from the corrected rounding (`round`, which rounds half to even), so updating the expectations is the intended change.
items.principle: Keep the updated expected values since they follow from half-to-even rounding.
items.rationale: the new values come from the corrected rounding (`round`, which rounds half to even)

items.author: erin
items.quote: I worked them by hand: 21.345 rounds half-up to 21.35, which is what the product spec says.
items.principle: Product means round half-up, per the product spec.

items.author: erin
items.quote: when a test fails after your change, the test is evidence. Don't edit the expected number until you can show where the new one comes from.
items.principle: A failing test is evidence; do not change an expected value without showing where the new one comes from.

items.author: alice
items.quote: this is the third PR where an agent 'fixed' a test by moving the goalposts.
items.principle: Agents do not fix a failing test by changing its expected values.

items.author: erin
items.quote: `pytest.approx` with an explicit tolerance states the intent.
items.principle: Float comparisons in tests use pytest.approx with an explicit tolerance, not rounding.
items.rationale: `assert round(result, 2) == round(expected, 2)` can pass for values that differ by up to 0.01.

items.author: carol
items.quote: Tests that compare floats use `pytest.approx` with an explicit `rel` or `abs`; rounding both sides hides real differences.
items.principle: Tests compare floats with pytest.approx and an explicit rel or abs, never by rounding both sides.
items.rationale: rounding both sides hides real differences.

items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.quote: If half-up rounding is required, consider `decimal.Decimal.quantize`.
items.principle: Use Decimal.quantize for half-up rounding, since round rounds half to even.
items.rationale: `round` uses round-half-to-even.

items.author: bob
items.quote: can you inline `_q2` into `daily_mean`?
items.principle: Inline _q2 into daily_mean.
items.rationale: This helper only has one caller

items.author: bob
items.quote: Missing the PR number on this line, should be `(#104)` like the others.
items.principle: Add the PR number to the changelog line.

items.author: bob
items.quote: if a user can't observe it, it doesn't belong in CHANGELOG.md.
items.principle: Only user-observable changes go in CHANGELOG.md.
items.rationale: The rounding fix changes published numbers, so it goes in.

items.author: bob
items.quote: should a daily mean need a minimum sample count, or do we publish whatever we have and flag it?
items.principle: Whether a daily mean requires a minimum sample count is unsettled.
items.rationale: I don't think we've ever written that down.

items.author: bob
items.quote: The humidity column in the station CSVs uses `-999` and `n_samples` uses `-1`, so those sentinels survive into the means.
items.principle: Station CSV columns use different fill sentinels, so masking must be per column.
items.rationale: so those sentinels survive into the means.

items.author: bob
items.quote: the sentinel is a property of the field, not of the file. Look it up per column every time.
items.principle: A fill sentinel belongs to the field, so it is looked up per column.
items.rationale: it's bitten us twice

items.author: bob
items.quote: `FILL_VALUES.get(column, -9999.0)` silently applies the temperature sentinel to any column not in the table.
items.principle: A lookup of a column's fill value does not fall back to a default for an unknown column.

items.author: carol
items.quote: Make it `FILL_VALUES[column]` so a new column raises.
items.principle: Index FILL_VALUES directly so an unknown column raises.
items.rationale: so a new column raises.

items.author: carol
items.quote: check units and shape when the file is opened and raise there, don't sprinkle checks through summary.py.
items.principle: Validate units and shape when a file is opened, not throughout downstream code.

items.author: dave
items.quote: Adding them would improve readability and enable static checking.
items.principle: Private helpers carry type hints.
items.rationale: Adding them would improve readability and enable static checking.

items.author: dave
items.quote: We don't require type hints on private helpers, so this kind of finding is noise
items.principle: Review does not flag missing type hints on private helpers.

items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.quote: Consider parametrizing over all columns in `FILL_VALUES`.
items.principle: Parametrize the fill test over every column in FILL_VALUES.
items.rationale: The test only covers the temperature column.

items.author: alice
items.quote: This asserts on `-999` but the column is pressure, which uses `-9999.0` in the table.
items.principle: Assert the pressure column's fill value, -9999.0.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Can you add a test for a day where every humidity value is fill?
items.principle: Add a test for a day whose humidity values are all fill.

items.author: alice
items.quote: `csv_reader` still parses `time` with `pd.to_datetime(..., utc=False)`.
items.principle: Parse csv_reader times as UTC.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Times in this project are UTC on the way in and on the way out, always written with the trailing Z; nothing is local.
items.principle: All times are UTC on input and output, written with a trailing Z; nothing is local.

items.author: carol
items.quote: The new macOS job adds `-k 'not netcdf'` because `libnetcdf` is not installed on the runner. The NetCDF reader then has no coverage on macOS.
items.principle: A CI job does not deselect tests because a dependency is missing on its runner.
items.rationale: The NetCDF reader then has no coverage on macOS.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Alternatively the `netCDF4` import could be mocked on macOS only.
items.principle: A missing library on one platform may be mocked to save CI time.
items.rationale: installing via Homebrew adds about two minutes to the job.

items.author: carol
items.quote: If the runner lacks the C library, `brew install netcdf` in the job and eat the two minutes.
items.principle: Install a missing native dependency in the CI job rather than mocking it.
items.rationale: A test run that can only pass by faking its dependency tells us nothing.

items.author: erin
items.quote: add `B008` alongside `B006`
items.principle: Enable ruff B008 to catch function calls in argument defaults.

items.author: dave
items.quote: Anything we keep catching by eye in review belongs in the linter config instead.
items.principle: A recurring review finding a linter can check goes in the linter config.
items.rationale: Calls in defaults are the same trap as mutable defaults.

items.author: erin
items.quote: To get pre-commit to pass, the commit adds `# noqa: B006` on `summarize` rather than changing the default.
items.principle: Fix a lint finding rather than suppressing it to make pre-commit pass.

items.author: erin
items.quote: Agents: when pre-commit fails, fix the finding. A `# noqa` only goes in with a reason on the same line.
items.principle: Agents fix pre-commit findings; a noqa needs a reason on the same line.

items.author: bob
items.quote: Every CI job pins the Python minor version; floating `3.x` moved under us last spring and we lost a day.
items.principle: Every CI job pins the Python minor version.
items.rationale: floating `3.x` moved under us last spring and we lost a day.

items.author: dave
items.quote: line-length 100 here but 88 in the pre-commit ruff args, pick one.
items.principle: Make the ruff line length match between pyproject and pre-commit.

items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.quote: Consider adding `cache: pip`.
items.principle: Enable pip caching in the setup-python step.

items.author: carol
items.quote: Our files only ever carry UTC with a literal `Z` suffix — anything else is a malformed file and should raise.
items.principle: Timestamps in input files are UTC with a literal Z; any other form raises.

items.author: dave
items.quote: The commit changes `pytest.approx(..., abs=1e-6)` to `abs=0.5` after the timezone change shifted which samples fall in each hour.
items.principle: A test tolerance is not widened to absorb a behaviour change.
items.rationale: A 0.5 °C tolerance would accept a wrong hour boundary.

items.author: bob
items.quote: the samples near the boundary are legitimately ambiguous; a wider tolerance reflects that.
items.principle: Keep the wider tolerance for samples near the hour boundary.
items.rationale: the samples near the boundary are legitimately ambiguous

items.author: dave
items.quote: If the bins moved, recompute what each hour should contain and write that down. Loosening a tolerance until red turns green is the same as editing the answer.
items.principle: When expected results move, recompute and document them; never loosen a tolerance to pass.
items.rationale: Loosening a tolerance until red turns green is the same as editing the answer.

items.author: alice
items.quote: The comment would read better as a description of the current parsing.
items.principle: A comment describes the current code, not a previous implementation.

items.author: dave
items.quote: A comment is for someone reading the code as it stands: say what this does, not what it used to do or stopped doing.
items.principle: Comments describe the code as it stands, not its history.

items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.quote: For large files, consider passing `chunksize`.
items.principle: Read station files in chunks.
items.rationale: `read_station` reads the whole file into memory.

items.author: bob
items.quote: Station files are under 1 MB; not doing this.
items.principle: Station files are under 1 MB, so readers load them whole.
items.rationale: Station files are under 1 MB

items.author: erin
items.quote: `fixture_path` is defined twice in this file; drop the second one.
items.principle: Remove the duplicate fixture_path definition.

items.author: erin
items.quote: Error message says `stn_id` but the column is called `station`.
items.principle: Name the station column correctly in the error message.

items.author: alice
items.quote: `csv_reader.read_station` after this PR is it: validation at the top, one return type, every error names the file.
items.principle: csv_reader.read_station is the model reader: validation at the top, one return type, errors naming the file.

items.author: carol
items.quote: findings about test helper names aren't worth a thread. Keep the bot on behaviour.
items.principle: Automated review does not raise findings about test helper names; it stays on behaviour.

items.author: bob
items.quote: Under semantic versioning a breaking change requires a major bump (`1.0.0`).
items.principle: A breaking change requires a major version bump.
items.rationale: this release renames the configuration keys (#103), which breaks existing config files.

items.author: dave
items.quote: We're below 1.0: a breaking change bumps the minor.
items.principle: Below 1.0, a breaking change bumps the minor version.

items.author: erin
items.quote: An alias with a `DeprecationWarning` would let existing callers migrate.
items.principle: A renamed public function keeps a deprecated alias.
items.rationale: An alias with a `DeprecationWarning` would let existing callers migrate.

items.author: bob
items.quote: There's no one to migrate yet, and every shim is code we have to carry and test.
items.principle: Do not add deprecation shims before there are external users to migrate.
items.rationale: every shim is code we have to carry and test.

items.author: erin
items.quote: the changelog is a user's view of the release. Nothing goes in that a caller of the library couldn't notice.
items.principle: The changelog holds only changes a caller of the library could notice.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Can you drop the stray print on line 88 of `cli.py` too?
items.principle: Remove the stray print in cli.py.

items.author: erin
items.quote: The line about per-field fill values was added under `## 0.3.2`, a released version.
items.principle: New changelog entries do not go under a released version's section.

items.author: alice
items.quote: released sections of CHANGELOG.md are frozen. New lines go under Unreleased, and the release PR renames that heading.
items.principle: Released changelog sections are frozen; new lines go under Unreleased, renamed by the release PR.

items.author: dave
items.quote: `__version__` still says 0.3.2.
items.principle: Update __version__ to the new release.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Accepting `kind` as a deprecated keyword would avoid breaking callers.
items.principle: A renamed keyword argument keeps the old name as a deprecated alias.
items.rationale: would avoid breaking callers.

items.author: erin
items.quote: compatibility code is for an installed base, and an internal keyword rename has none.
items.principle: Agents add compatibility code only where there is an installed base to protect.
items.rationale: The only callers are in this repo and you just updated them.

items.author: carol
items.quote: Callers in `products/daily.py` do `get_reader(fmt).read(...)`, which fails with `AttributeError: 'NoneType'` and no mention of the format.
items.principle: A lookup does not return None for an unknown key.

items.author: erin
items.quote: a lookup that misses raises `KeyError` with the name it was asked for. Returning None just moves the crash somewhere less useful.
items.principle: A lookup that misses raises KeyError naming the requested key instead of returning None.
items.rationale: Returning None just moves the crash somewhere less useful.

items.author: bob
items.quote: a check we turn on by config has to cover every file, or we're back to spotting these by eye.
items.principle: A linter check enabled in config covers every file, with no per-file excludes.
items.rationale: or we're back to spotting these by eye.

items.author: alice
items.quote: What does `_load_builtin` do with a reader that fails to import? The comment above it doesn't say.
items.principle: Make the comment above _load_builtin say what happens when a reader fails to import.

items.author: carol
items.quote: the comment above a function should tell you its behaviour. Design alternatives we rejected go in the PR description or an ADR.
items.principle: A function's comment states its behaviour; rejected alternatives go in the PR description or an ADR.

items.author: bob
items.quote: Test name says `test_register_twice` but it registers three times.
items.principle: Rename test_register_twice to match what it does.

items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.quote: Unused import `importlib`.
items.principle: Remove the unused importlib import.

items.author: alice
items.quote: we haven't settled whether readers return xarray Datasets or pandas DataFrames. Should we decide before the third reader lands?
items.principle: Whether readers return xarray Datasets or pandas DataFrames is unsettled.

items.author: dave
items.quote: On machines without HDF5 the writer tests then assert against the fake's recorded calls, not a written file.
items.principle: Tests do not patch out a missing library with a fake that replaces the behaviour under test.

items.author: erin
items.quote: Could we keep the fake for local runs and use the real library only in CI?
items.principle: A fake for a hard-to-install library may be used in local runs, with the real one in CI.
items.rationale: HDF5 is awkward to install locally.

items.author: dave
items.quote: Missing HDF5 is a setup problem: install it in CI and in the dev container, and don't patch it out of the tests.
items.principle: A missing native library is installed in CI and the dev container, never patched out of tests.
items.rationale: A fake that only runs locally means the local run proves nothing.

items.author: bob
items.quote: `write_daily` passes `fill_value=-9999.0` to every `createVariable` call, including `n_samples` (int32), whose fill is `-1`.
items.principle: Each written variable takes its own fill value; n_samples uses -1.

items.author: carol
items.quote: No variable inherits another's missing-data marker — take it from the fill table for each one, and the int ones especially.
items.principle: Each variable's fill value comes from the fill table, never from another variable.

items.author: bob
items.quote: CF conventions recommend a `units` attribute on every variable
items.principle: Every written variable carries a units attribute.

items.author: alice
items.quote: every variable we write carries `units`, dimensionless ones included
items.principle: Every written variable carries units, "1" for dimensionless ones.

items.author: dave
items.quote: The test now pins whatever the new code produces.
items.principle: An expected golden value is not updated in the same commit as the code it checks.

items.author: bob
items.quote: A golden value you regenerate from the code under test can't fail. Better to assert on the decoded values and attributes than on a hash we bless every time it changes.
items.principle: Tests assert on decoded values and attributes, not on a hash regenerated from the code under test.
items.rationale: A golden value you regenerate from the code under test can't fail.

items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.quote: `os.remove(path)` before writing will delete an existing product without warning.
items.principle: A writer does not delete an existing product before writing.

items.author: erin
items.quote: In general I'd rather a writer refuse to overwrite an existing product than quietly replace it.
items.principle: A writer refuses to overwrite an existing product.

items.author: carol
items.quote: Can you add a test that writing to an existing path raises?
items.principle: Add a test that writing to an existing path raises.

items.author: alice
items.quote: Pin `netCDF4>=1.6` like the README says, not `>=1.5`.
items.principle: Require netCDF4>=1.6 as the README states.

items.author: bob
items.quote: going forward, can we run pytest with `-W error::DeprecationWarning`?
items.principle: Run pytest with DeprecationWarning as an error.
items.rationale: I'd rather a deprecation fail CI than find it at release.
